set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Turn up and right, following the trail as it parallels the cliff to a small scree field between the Lower and Upper Replica. Cross it, follow the trail past the Upper Replica to another short scree field, and continue up the hill to the left. The first route you reach is Boy Scout Hand Grenade, and the rest are off a small ledge with a few trees further up the hill. Blues Riff is the leftmost line on the Bud Wall, just past the corner from Boy Scout Hand Grenade.

review.notes: Area pages: trail from the meadow; route page: far left side of the wall. Bolted anchor; no descent stated.

set.approach: The wall lies below Shish Kabob and one way in is down the descent gully, taking the easiest line past Run Ross Run and Red October and downclimbing a chockstone boulder problem, and leaving it on skier's right when you can. A faint trail may trace the wall, rising briefly and then dropping past several routes on the right. Groove to It follows the obvious water runnel.
set.descent_text: Lower or rappel from the anchors; some routes on this wall need a long rope to lower or double ropes to rappel.

review.notes: Area page: approach and wall-level lowering/rappel note; route page: obvious water runnel. Rope lengths left out.

set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Rather than climbing the trail to the right, turn left across a small scree slide to the short cliff beneath the tall, roofed wall (Sweden). Love Your Shotgun is the first route you meet. Chai in my eye is on the cliff's left end, beyond a patch of nettles.
set.descent_text: Lower off from the anchors at the top of the bolts.

review.notes: Area pages: trail; route page: left end across the nettle patch, bolts to lower-offs.

set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Colossus starts a bit left of the big gold streak that marks the middle of the wall; its first bolts are left of a distinct chert feature in the streak.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: left of the gold streak. No descent stated.

set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. The first route you reach on the cliff is The Bowl of Heaven. This route is short, with a chain anchor.

review.notes: Area page: approach. Route page gives no placement on the wall, so only the crag access is written; the route is named like its crag, so identity is medium. No descent stated.

set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Silver Trembling Hands starts along the right edge of the big gold streak at the wall's center.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: right side of the gold streak. No descent stated.

set.approach: At the signed pass, turn south onto the Bridger Ridge Trail. A short way along, keep left to stay on the ridge (the right fork drops to the Bridger Foothills), and follow the trail south and then southwest around its switchbacks. Just before it swings southeast and gets steeper, you reach a rocky outcrop; step off the trail and walk along the outcrop's foot to the climbs. Bury The Hatchet is the first route met when you move along the wall left to right, starting in a dihedral beside a pine on its left.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: first route left to right, dihedral left of a pine. No descent stated.

set.approach: At the signed pass, turn south onto the Bridger Ridge Trail. A short way along, keep left to stay on the ridge, and follow the trail south and then southwest around its switchbacks. Just before it swings southeast and gets steeper, you reach a rocky outcrop; step off the trail and walk along the outcrop's foot to the climbs. Goodwill Jeans is on a wall set slightly back and right of the main Murphy's Wall; scramble to the foot of a mid-sized crack to begin.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: wall behind and right of the main wall, scramble to a crack. No descent stated.

set.approach: Cross the meadow on the climbers trail, heading directly to the Lower Replica, the first big triangular cliff you meet. Trails to every other cliff at the crag fork from its base. Take the trail left toward Sweden and Denmark, follow the faint trail to the ledge underneath Sweden's big roofs and continue beyond into the next scree drainage. Traverse the scree until the wall is visible up the hill to the right, then follow a narrow drainage up through a small constriction to the base. There may be a fixed hand line to aid a loose fourth-class section there. The approach is loose, so wear a helmet and watch your footing and rockfall. The View starts on the right side of the wall.

review.notes: Area pages: approach; route page: begins on the right side of the wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Bozeman, take the South Brackett Creek road to a gate on the left side, and park along the roadside across from it. Walk the road up toward the saddle, but cut right before reaching the top and hug the base of the mountain. Gain the ridge line, then keep hugging the foot of the mountain around the peak, through tall plants. Drop into the bowl full of large boulders and head to the top of the snowfield, where most climbs start. The only water near the base is the seasonal snowfield, so bring your own supply. Pauli Wants a Cracker is to the left of Trial by Fire and Blue Phoenix, on the face directly left of the conspicuous dihedral that faces right.
set.descent_text: Hiking down the peak is long and loose. From the summit, look for small cairns leading down through the chossy terrain, and if you lose them aim for the saddle. Cliffs can appear suddenly, and the sharp rock is hard on shoes and feet. After the saddle there is still a long hike out.

review.notes: Area page: approach and descent from the summit; route page: location, and the last pitch continuing to the summit. Times and distances left out.

set.approach: Bikes or e-bikes are very useful for the approach. Begin where the Upper Brackett Creek trail meets the Fairy Lake road (FS500); you get to that junction from either the Battle Ridge trailhead or Fairy Lake. Walk south on the Upper Brackett Creek trail to an open meadow on the right, turn right into it and continue southwest on intermittent game and cow trails. Through the trees, a steep meadow appears on the right; hike up it to the base of a bluff in front of the Wave, then walk southwest around the bluff and uphill to the base of the climbs. Fair Spanish Ladies is right of center on the central apron of rock.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, and knot the ends of the rope.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: right side of the center apron, rappel the route. Rope length left out. Distances left out.

set.approach: Bikes or e-bikes are very useful for the approach. Begin where the Upper Brackett Creek trail meets the Fairy Lake road (FS500); you get to that junction from either the Battle Ridge trailhead or Fairy Lake. Walk south on the Upper Brackett Creek trail to an open meadow on the right, turn right into it and continue southwest on intermittent game and cow trails. Through the trees, a steep meadow appears on the right; hike up it to the base of a bluff in front of the Wave, then walk southwest around the bluff and uphill to the base of the climbs. Climb the broken apron on its left until you can easily traverse right to a belay at a good ledge holding a bush.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, and tie knots in the ends of the rope. The ledge with the bush is not always reached by a single rope, so expect some easy downclimbing to a smaller ledge a little above it.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: start and rappel descent. Rappel count and rope length left out.
